summary: Created the ordinary `helpdesk` account on node1. It can restart only `sshd` through passwordless sudo; arbitrary commands, shells, and other service restarts are denied. Configuration and functionality persisted across the required node reboot.
actions_performed: Created `helpdesk` with a private group and home directory; it is not in an administrative group.
Installed a root-owned, mode-0440 sudoers rule limited to `/usr/bin/systemctl restart sshd` and `sshd.service`.
Validated sudoers syntax and tested allowed and denied operations.
Restarted node1 once and verified boot identity, SSH health, account data, and permissions afterward.

evidence.requirement: Create a non-administrative helpdesk account with narrowly scoped sudo
evidence.summary: Shows the ordinary account, exact sudoers rule, secure ownership/mode, valid syntax, and effective command list.
Before and after reboot, helpdesk successfully restarted SSH; the PID changed and SSH remained active with a live OpenSSH banner.

evidence.requirement: Helpdesk has no other administrative privileges
evidence.summary: Policy permits the SSH restart while denying root identity execution, a root shell, and restarting another service.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 7ef78016-ba83-4481-867b-e5a349df1b54, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID abd221c3-5314-4652-8e03-bd06fa5833d4, full system/SSH/account/policy recovery, and a successful post-reboot helpdesk restart.
